note: Swapping granodiorite for quartz monzonite needs a geology source naming this place. USGS PP 470 names 'Buttermilk Country' three times, never its rock; USGS OFR 82-380 covers the Buttermilk Roadless Area UPSLOPE (7,700-8,700 ft, the boulders are at ~6,400 ft) and says till of 'variety of rock types'. Wikipedia's quartz-monzonite sentence cites a geotechnical company's marketing blog (no author, no sources). Sub-areas with no rock left unfilled. MAP READING (inference): on USGS PP 470 pl. 2 nearly every wall plots on Kt, Tungsten Hills quartz monzonite bedrock - none on a granodiorite unit (see mapReading). Bateman maps no till under the main boulder knobs, only under the 'Buttermilk Country' label to the SW.

quote: The member is named for Battleship Rock, which is also designated the type section ... a succession of ash flows that are in part welded.
note: USGS Bulletin 1274-P (Bailey, Smith & Ross 1969), p. P17-P18. Battleship Rock is the TYPE SECTION of the rhyolitic ash-flow Battleship Rock Member (now Battleship Rock Ignimbrite); the same text calls it 'Battleship Rock welded tuff'. Welding is 'in part' - 'tuff' is the conservative alternative if partial welding matters. The held 'limestone (mapped)' matches the unit's BASE: 'at Battleship Rock the unit rests unconformably on red beds of the Abo Formation (Permian) and on fossiliferous limestones of the Magdalena Group'. The one MP route (Battleship Direct) climbs the prow arete of the 200-ft formation.

quote: Gray, porphyritic-aphanitic dacite. ... Potassium-argon radiometric age of Bishop Peak is 24.9 ± 0.2 m.y.
note: USGS MF-686 sheet 2 (Hall & Prior 1975, 1:24,000) maps the Bishop Peak plug as Td 'Dacite' and its legend names Bishop Peak under that unit; the quote is TRANSCRIBED from the scanned plate image (no text layer). True Summit Blocks' own page puts it at 'The very top of Bishop peak', inside the Td body, hence the exception. None of the 12 MP boulder pages names a rock ('Sadie' has no MP page under this area). MAP READING (inference, decides nothing): plotting each boulder's MP GPS on the georeferenced plate (frame corners 120d45'/35d22.5' and 120d45'/35d15'; the MP summit point lands on the map's 1546 summit within ~50 m), Wild Wild Western Pinnacles falls inside the Td plug; Boulder Under the Shrub and Hummingbird Boulders fall on the plug's eastern contact; Chlorissa, Pete, Mini Ball, Boulder In The Woods, Trail Boulder and The Traverse Boulder fall on Qls landslide deposits ('rock and mudflow debris composed of material from source rocks upslope') just east of the plug, i.e. most likely dacite blocks shed from it; The Potato and The Lost Dog Boulder (the held-greenstone pair) fall 70-90 m north of the plug's northern contact, where Qls and KJfmv ('metavolcanic rocks, primarily greenstone') meet. No sandstone unit is mapped near any boulder. Georeferencing error is roughly 50 m, comparable to some boulders' distance from the contact.
